summary: CLI SSO failing for remote engineers behind NAT/VPN due to Okta session IP binding
summary_alternate: Okta session context tied to client IP invalidates CLI OAuth flow when users switch networks
description:
Issue summary: Several remote engineers are unable to complete the CLI SSO flow when connecting from home networks or corporate VPNs that perform NAT. The Okta session appears to be bound to the original client IP and SSO token validation fails when the CLI exchange happens from a different outbound IP.

Impact: Multiple developers cannot authenticate with the redwood CLI to access internal tools, blocking deployments, debug access, and daily workflows. Not customer-facing but high internal impact.

Environment: Production Okta org (redwood.okta.com), redwood CLI v0.9.3, macOS and Linux clients, users primarily behind home NAT or enterprise VPNs that use shared egress IPs.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Run 'redwood login --sso' from a machine behind a NATed network (home router or corporate VPN egress)
3) The CLI opens the browser and completes the Okta web flow successfully (browser shows authenticated),
4) The browser redirects to localhost callback; CLI attempts to exchange the code for tokens, but returns an error 'token_validation_failed: ip_mismatch'
5) Repeating the flow from a different network (e.g., mobile hotspot) allows successful login for the same user.
observed_behavior: Browser-based SSO completes, but CLI fails to accept the OAuth code/token. Okta logs show session context includes the original client IP, and token exchange is rejected when observed IP differs from the stored context.
expected_behavior: CLI SSO should work regardless of transient IP changes during the browser-based flow (common when using Wi-Fi -> VPN or NATed egress).
logs: Okta System Log excerpt (2026-03-10T09:13:22Z): eventType=oauth2.token.failed reason=ip_mismatch sessionId=00abc123
redwood-cli debug output: ERR: token exchange failed: token_validation_failed (ip_mismatch)
Browser console: callback received code=0A1B2C; callback served to http://localhost:54321/callback
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Maya Chen: Initial report from two engineers in #internal-auth. They can authenticate in browser but the CLI errors out immediately after redirect. Sharing screenshots in thread.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Luis Ortega: Assigned to me for triage. I can reproduce locally when I force an egress IP change during the flow. Adding SRE and Security.

2026-03-10 13:20 - Priya Kapoor (SRE): Checked cloudfront and gateway logs — callback hits the callback server from an IP that matches the browser, but token exchange from CLI comes from different IP (due to VPN exit node). Okta rejects with ip_mismatch in system log.
2026-03-10 15:40 - Andrew Park (Security): Need to confirm whether Okta org has 'enforce session IP binding' enabled for OIDC flows. If so, this was likely tightened in Feb org settings.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Luis Ortega: Reproduced across macOS and Ubuntu. Workaround: users can use the browser-based API token page (console) to generate a long-lived token, but that's suboptimal. Filing Okta support ticket.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Maya Chen: Okta Support replied: behavior caused by 'session cookie enforcement' for SSO flows; recommended either change the RPT (relying party trust) to not bind IP or update the client to perform PKCE + same-origin callback without new egress change. Security is reviewing.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Andrew Park: Security approved a temporary relaxation for internal 'redwood-cli' OIDC app: allow token exchange when user agent session present and IP changes detected from known NAT ranges. Ops to apply in staging first.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Luis Ortega: Implemented CLI retry logic for a short window (60s) to re-attempt token exchange and validate the session; testing in staging now.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Okta session context binds the web session to the client IP at the time of authentication. Because the CLI opens the browser on the user's machine but the actual token exchange is routed through the CLI which may have different egress (VPN or NAT), Okta treats the exchange as suspicious and rejects it.

Findings: Okta system logs consistently show 'ip_mismatch' for failed exchanges. The problem frequency spikes for users using enterprise VPNs that route CLI traffic through a shared egress IP. Local reproduction succeeds when network egress is switched mid-flow.

Temporary mitigations tested: (1) guide users to run the CLI flow while not connected to VPN, (2) generate a console token via browser and use CLI --token. Both are acceptable short-term but hurt productivity.

Longer-term options: update Okta app config to relax IP binding for redwood-cli OIDC client; or change CLI to perform the entire OAuth flow in the browser and pass tokens back via secure websocket/proxy that preserves the same egress IP; or rotate to a PKCE flow that Okta treats differently. Security prefers minimal changes to org-wide enforcement; suggests scoped relaxation for the internal CLI app only.
resolution:
(work in progress) Temporary: internal doc posted in #internal-auth with workarounds (disconnect VPN during flow or generate console token). Okta support ticket opened (SR-611892).

Planned permanent fix: Ops will apply a scoped relaxation on the 'redwood-cli' OIDC client configuration in staging for a 2-week pilot, while Engineering implements CLI-side PKCE+loopback flow improvements (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/418). After pilot validation, Security will approve production rollout.

Follow-ups: create INT task to update runbook and add e2e tests for CLI SSO behavior across NAT/VPN (INT-24641 created).
